stem: An HPC cluster running tightly coupled MPI simulations across many EC2 instances in one Availability Zone needs the lowest possible inter-node latency plus an OS-bypass low-latency transport for collective communication.

choices.text: A partition placement group with enhanced networking (ENA)
Graviton instances with no placement group
A cluster placement group with EFA

rationale: A cluster placement group packs instances into one Availability Zone on the same high-bisection-bandwidth network segment for the lowest possible latency, and EFA adds the OS-bypass, low-latency transport that MPI-style collective communication needs beyond what ordinary enhanced networking provides. A partition placement group with ENA isolates hardware failures across racks for large distributed systems like HDFS, not the lowest possible latency between tightly coupled nodes. A spread placement group places a small number of instances on genuinely distinct hardware to avoid a shared failure domain, which does not give this cluster the tightest possible network proximity. Graviton instances change the processor architecture and price-performance, not network proximity or transport, and without a placement group the instances have no guaranteed proximity to each other at all.
